mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces equity discount rates, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines over the prior month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 6.0% for two consecutive months, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that increase recession risk and depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0% for two consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 in 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in RSAFS (consumer credit demand) and rise in FEDFUNDS (monetary tightening) signals reduced credit availability and higher borrowing costs that depress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when RSAFS declines and FEDFUNDS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion, a sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity that precedes market correction, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 in 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A rising housing starts (HOUST) indicates improving consumer confidence and economic activity that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 1.5% for three consecutive months, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 1.5% for three consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 in 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rise in industrial production (INDPRO) signals labor-market supply mismatch that indicates economic instability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS declines and INDPRO rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 in 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high labor market tightness (UNRATE < 4.5%), a rising payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong job growth that boosts consumer spending and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 in 3-year windows.
